explanation: An empty String has capacity 0 and allocates nothing, yet c_str() is "". Capacity grows 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4; appending 5 characters to 3 needs 8 = max(2 * 4, 8); appending 2 more needs 10 > 8, so the capacity becomes max(16, 10) = 16. One allocation per growth: 5.

String("hello") allocates exactly 5 characters (plus the '\0'). A copy has its own buffer, so changing it leaves the original alone. Moving takes the buffer: no allocation, and the source is left empty with capacity 0.
find returns the first match at or after pos, or npos (-1). substr(pos, npos) runs to the end; substr(size(), n) is ""; pos > size() throws std::out_of_range.
No String with capacity 0 allocates; c_str() of every empty String is a valid "".
String(s) and String(count, ch) allocate exactly the characters they hold.
c_str()[size()] is '\0' after every operation (clear, push_back, reserve, append, String(n, ch)).
Each buffer holds capacity() + 1 bytes: the characters plus the terminating '\0'.
Capacity doubles: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64; 7 allocations for 40 push_backs.
The new capacity is max(2 * capacity(), size() + n): 2 -> 4 -> 12 -> 24 -> 48.
From capacity 0, appending 10 characters needs exactly 10.
reserve(n) reallocates to exactly n only when n > capacity() and never shrinks. Filling the reserved space does not allocate.
clear() keeps the buffer and the capacity.
A copy owns its own buffer of exactly size() characters (not the source's capacity).
After a = b, a holds its own copy of b's characters, whether it had more or fewer before.
s = s leaves s unchanged.
Move assignment frees the target's buffer, takes the source's without allocating, and leaves the source empty with capacity 0 and still usable.
s = std::move(s) leaves s unchanged.
A moved-from String is empty, has capacity 0, and is fully usable.
The destructor frees the buffer exactly once.
A String may hold '\0' characters (shown as _): size() counts them, and copying, appending a String and comparing use all size() characters, not strlen or strcmp.
find and substr also see past a '\0'; append(const char*) stops at the first '\0'.
s.append(s) and s += s work even when they reallocate: the old characters must be read before the old buffer is freed.
append(c_str() + k) on the same String must work when it reallocates.
Lexicographic order; a proper prefix is less; the empty string is less than any other.
substr(pos, count) takes min(count, size() - pos) characters; npos and other huge counts must not overflow pos + count.
A non-empty substr allocates exactly once (an empty one not at all) and frees it when destroyed.

find returns the first position >= pos, or npos. An empty needle is found at pos when pos <= size(). A needle longer than the rest of the string is never found (watch for size() - needle.size() underflowing).
